title: Garlic and Rosemary Crusted Roast Beef
changes_from_base: Coated after searing with a rosemary, garlic, lemon zest and chilli paste, roasted over whole garlic cloves and finished with a short blast at 250 °C to crisp the herb crust; served without Yorkshire puddings or gravy.
summary: This follows the same slow-roast method as our classic roast beef, but the joint is coated in a rosemary, garlic, lemon and chilli paste, roasted over whole garlic cloves, then blasted at high heat to crisp the herb crust — served simply, without puddings or gravy.
equipment: roasting tin with a wire rack
pestle and mortar or small food processor

ingredients.item: beef topside or eye-of-round roasting joint, tied
fine sea salt or table salt
whole garlic bulb, cloves separated, skin on

steps.title: Dry-brine the joint
steps.text: The day before, or at least 4 hours ahead, pat the beef dry and rub it all over with the fine salt. Set it on a rack over a tray and refrigerate uncovered, which lets the salt season the meat deeply and dries the surface ready for browning.

steps.title: Make the herb paste
steps.text: Crush or blitz the rosemary, grated garlic, olive oil, lemon zest, chilli flakes and black pepper to a coarse green paste. Crushing the rosemary and garlic this way releases their aromatic oils, so the paste tastes punchy rather than just chopped.

steps.title: Sear, then coat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 120°C (100°C fan). Pat the beef dry, rub with half the neutral oil, then brown it in the remaining hot oil in a frying pan over high heat for 2-3 minutes a side, until coloured all over. Let it cool for 10 minutes, then spread the paste thickly over the top and sides; searing first means the garlic in the paste roasts gently rather than catching and burning.

steps.title: Roast low and rest
steps.text: Set the joint on a rack in the roasting tin with the whole garlic cloves and rosemary sprigs scattered underneath, and roast for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, until a probe thermometer in the centre reads 60°C. Tent loosely with foil and rest for 20 minutes, during which the temperature continues to climb.

steps.title: Crisp the crust and serve
steps.text: Heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan), then uncover the beef and return it for 6-8 minutes, until the herb crust is crisp and fragrant and the centre reads at least 63°C on the probe thermometer. Rest for a further 3 minutes, then carve thinly across the grain and serve with the soft roasted garlic squeezed from its skins.

tips: Let the beef cool briefly before adding the paste — spreading it onto a scorching-hot joint straight from searing can singe the garlic before it even reaches the oven.
Don't skip the final high-heat blast; it's what turns the soft herb coating into a crisp, fragrant crust.
Check the centre temperature with a probe rather than guessing by time, since joints vary in shape and thickness.
Squeeze the roasted garlic cloves straight from their skins over the sliced beef — they turn soft and sweet during roasting.
storage: Carved beef keeps in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat slices gently, covered, in a low oven or in a pan with a splash of stock until piping hot throughout (74°C); this joint doesn't freeze well once roasted, as the crust loses its crispness. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
